title: Consensus at Three Thresholds
description: threshold.py runs the same consensus task at three distance thresholds and prints the cluster count and the start of the synthesis for each. The config file stays unchanged.

steps.description: The script imports `load_config` and `run_consensus` from `lab4`, loads the config, and defines one long-form question and three thresholds: `0.1`, `0.3`, and `0.5`, labeled tight, medium, and loose.
The loop walks the thresholds and sets `config["consensus"]["distance_threshold"]` before each run. The page notes this changes the value in memory only, so `config.json` stays as it was.
`run_consensus` returns the synthesis, drafts, labels, representatives, and call count. `num_clusters` counts the distinct labels, which is the number of positions the drafts formed.
Each pass prints the threshold, the cluster count, and the first 200 characters of the synthesis, so you can compare the output across the three dial settings.

steps.question: The page says each threshold makes seven calls, six samples and one synthesis, so the run makes how many in total?
